page: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a 5th-generation compute-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon 8275CL processor using x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration delivers 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB L1d cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 16 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio that fits standard compute-intensive provisioning profiles. Advanced hardware flags include support for AVX-512 foundation instructions, AES cryptography, FMA, and BMI2 bit manipulation.

Performance evaluation reveals consistent mid-range execution across core microbenchmarks. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1494.09 and a multi-core score of 7865.45, alongside a Geekbench multi-core rating of 4531. Memory bandwidth tests measured 50.41 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 38.06 GB/sec for uncached writes. The instance performs well in web application tasks, recording 7.26 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 7.77 million operations/sec in Redis SET workloads. Conversely, benchmark performance drops into lower tiers for demanding natural language processing tasks, such as 7B LLM prompt processing at 11.09 tokens/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 28.28 GB/sec.

The c5.2xlarge provides a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation and includes no local ephemeral storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data requirements. The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio presents strong resource density for tasks where processing power is prioritized over large memory footprints, keeping compute unit costs efficient for targeted workloads. This profile makes the instance well suited for stateless web servers, CI/CD code compilation pipelines, data transformation tasks, and general CPU-bound processing, while remaining constrained for large-scale machine learning inference or memory-heavy database deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a 5th-generation compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon 8275CL processor. It provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache and 16 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, resulting in a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The architecture includes support for instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 foundation, AES, and BMI2. In benchmark testing, the c5.2xlarge demonstrates middle-tier performance across general compute tasks, achieving 7.26 GB/sec in static web serving and 7.77 million operations/sec in Redis SET operations. However, performance degrades on memory-intensive LLM prompt processing and multi-threaded decompression tasks. With no included local storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, this instance offers a cost-effective allocation model for CPU-intensive stateless workloads, high-concurrency web applications, software compilation, and general batch processing jobs that do not require heavy local storage or large memory allocations.
